person.name: Alan Mathison Turing
person.summary: English pioneer of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence whose wartime codebreaking and foundational work on computation reshaped modern technology.

portrait.caption: Alan Turing at age 16 (1930), photographed at Sherborne School.
portrait.alt: Portrait of Alan Turing as a 16-year-old student in a suit and tie.

events.title: Birth in Maida Vale
events.description: Alan Mathison Turing was born in Maida Vale, London, to Julius Mathison Turing and Ethel Sara Turing while his father was serving in the Indian Civil Service.

events.title: Sherborne School Enrollment
events.description: Turing enrolled at Sherborne School in Dorset; his determination to attend during the 1926 General Strike, bicycling roughly 60 miles to school, foreshadowed his persistence in scholarly pursuits.

events.title: Scholarship to King's College, Cambridge
events.description: Turing earned a scholarship to King's College, Cambridge, beginning undergraduate studies that culminated in first-class honours in mathematics and a fellowship for his work on probability theory.

events.title: On Computable Numbers Manuscript
events.description: Turing completed his seminal paper "On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem," introducing the concept of a universal computing machine and proving the undecidability of the Entscheidungsproblem.

events.title: Doctorate at Princeton University
events.description: Turing earned his PhD from Princeton University under Alonzo Church, publishing "Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals" and advancing ideas about oracle machines and relative computation.

events.title: Arrival at Bletchley Park
events.description: The day after Britain declared war on Germany, Turing reported to Bletchley Park to join the Government Code and Cypher School, beginning his pivotal role in Allied cryptanalysis.

events.title: First Bombe Installed
events.description: Following Turing's design work on mechanized Enigma decryption, the first operational bombe was installed, dramatically accelerating the decryption of German naval communications.

events.title: Automatic Computing Engine Proposal
events.description: At the National Physical Laboratory, Turing presented the first full specification for the Automatic Computing Engine (ACE), a pioneering stored-program computer design.

events.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
events.description: Turing published "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" in Mind, proposing the imitation game (later known as the Turing test) as a criterion for machine intelligence.

events.title: Conviction for Gross Indecency
events.description: After acknowledging a relationship with Arnold Murray, Turing was convicted of gross indecency and accepted chemical castration as an alternative to imprisonment, leading to the loss of his security clearance.

events.title: Death in Wilmslow
events.description: Turing died from cyanide poisoning at his home in Wilmslow; an inquest ruled the death a suicide, though later scholarship has debated the verdict.

events.title: UK Government Apology
events.description: Prime Minister Gordon Brown issued an official apology for the government's treatment of Turing, acknowledging the injustice of his prosecution and its impact on his life.

events.title: Royal Pardon Granted
events.description: Queen Elizabeth II granted Turing a posthumous royal pardon for his 1952 conviction, formally recognizing his contributions and the injustice he faced.

events.title: Portrait on Bank of England £50 Note
events.description: On the centenary of his birth, the Bank of England released a new polymer £50 note featuring Turing, highlighting his lasting legacy in computing and wartime codebreaking.
